candidates.title: CIA Stargate psychic spy program
candidates.quote: Paul worked in the CIA's Stargate project. Stargate was a psychic spy program that ran from 1972 to 1995.

link.reason: Both describe the CIA's Stargate psychic spy program, which ran from 1972 to 1995.
link.difference: Introduces Paul Smith as someone who worked in the program.

candidates.title: Ingo Swann remote views a shielded detector for Hal Puthoff
candidates.quote: In 1972, laser physicist Hal Puthoff was doing experiments with New York City-based psychic Ingo Swann.

link.reason: Both describe Ingo Swann affecting a shielded detector in Hal Puthoff's early-1970s experiments.
link.difference: Told by the host rather than by Puthoff firsthand. Dates it to 1972 and calls Swann New York City-based.

candidates.title: Rosemary Smith locates downed TU-22 spy plane
candidates.quote: And she essentially made a circle on the map, and it was a 3-square-mile area, and the plane was inside that.

link.reason: Both describe Rosemary Smith remote-viewing the downed Tu-22 in Zaire during Carter's presidency.
link.difference: Paul Smith tells it secondhand, credits Dale Graff, dates it to 1979 and adds the 3-square-mile circle drawn on the map.

candidates.title: Paul Smith remote views the USS Stark attack
candidates.quote: I started describing this vessel, which reminded me of an American destroyer.

link.reason: No story covers Paul Smith remote-viewing the 1987 USS Stark attack. It is a distinct incident.

candidates.title: Founding of the PEAR lab by Bob Jahn
candidates.quote:
The PEAR lab was started in 1979
by the dean of the engineering school, a guy named Bob Jahn.

link.reason: The founding of the PEAR lab in 1979 is one event. The nearest stories cover Jahn's whole career and his decades of random event generator research, which are broader.

candidates.title: PEAR random event generator results
candidates.quote: So the the final sort of chart of the PEAR data is this beautiful graph that kind of shows pretty definitively that the subjects were able to do what they were tasked to do.

link.reason: Both describe the PEAR lab's random event generator research under Bob Jahn at Princeton from 1979 onward, and both draw on Herb Mertz's account.
link.difference: Told by Mertz himself. Credits Brenda Dunne and the books Margins of Reality and Consciousness, the Source of Reality, and says the final chart shows a definitive effect.
